item.title: Show HN: Gasfree.app a Rack of Synthetizers in the Browser (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
item.description: Some years ago Moog released the Subharmonicon. I wanted so badly to try it but I didnt have the money to buy it, so I decided to code one myself. using Web Audio API. The end product wasnt great (there were lots of features missing) but it helped me pass the GAS (Gear Adquisition Syndrome). Fast forward to now. The other day I asked Claude to finish the project adding the missing features, and it did an amazing job, not only nailed the synth, but also improved the design so it looks closer to the original. After that I had to ask: - can it do other synths ?-, and I've been asking him for clones of famous synths I always wanted to try, just by passing the user manual, and it works!. The results are not always spot on, but at least you have something to play when money runs dry. I ended up adding some extra features (like timeline sequencer, FX, MIDI support). You can even construct your own synth using a node based interface! I released it on github in case other people want to extend the pool of synths. Enjoy it! Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50216770 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

item.title: Show HN: Corgi, a helpful {agent, terminal} multiplexer (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
item.description: Hey everyone, Inspired by Herdr, I've built an agent multiplexer that I've been using as my daily driver for a few weeks now. I think I improved on the concept in a few ways, focusing on the ergonomics I always wished I had: I show you what the agents are up to, along with a running feed of their activity. There's also a simple shortcut (F1) to go to the next unread agent. I use multiple accounts, so I've added unified launcher for Codex/Claude Code/Pi. Theres some careful ergonomics there: fast search and resume over sessions, inline usage tracking etc. Many small quality of life improvements to the terminal experience: - Links can be copied with a click, so no need to drag-select over many lines - cmd+v just pastes images (even on SSH) - images have a thumbnail preview. - Built-in CPU/Memory/GPU usage tracking, broken down by workspace I assume you have access to cheap inference (Luna/Haiku/etc). It just reuses the agents to organize things for you: what is this http link? what is this worktree about? what is each agent doing? It's small but it made my environment feel more cozy. On a personal note, I've been on a frustrating sick leave for a while now. I created Corgi to challenge myself, and see if I can go back. The answer is more mixed than I had hoped, but I am happy with the result and thankful for the experience. I hope you like it! a few friends & myself have been using it for a few weeks and it's been pretty nice. There's still a lot to improve and some rough edges, so feedback would be greatly appreciated. Thank you :) Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50214373 Points: 14 # Comments: 1
